user.title: SB Scheduler
user.description:
Day types are named rules about which dates count — Workday, Holiday, Day Off, Trash Day — that schedules run on. Each one can be shown in the calendar panel.

Give a country code and Holiday, Workday (Mon–Fri minus holidays) and Day Off (Mon–Fri minus workdays) are created for you, computed here with no other integration. Leave it empty to start with just Daily and Weekend.

data.holidays_country: Country for holidays (ISO code, e.g. US)

abort.single_instance_allowed: SB Scheduler is already set up.

add.title: Add a day type
add.description:
A day type is a rule about which dates count. Start from weekdays, holidays, calendars, typed dates, or another day type; subtract other day types; then optionally narrow it to a cadence or an ordinal.

Precedence is Always › Cancelled › Sources. Dates accept single days and ranges: 2026-12-25, 2027-06-05..2027-08-17

sources.name: Sources — where the dates come from

data.holidays_observed: Holidays: shift weekend holidays to the observed weekday

data_description.weekdays: Leave empty if the day type comes entirely from holidays, a calendar or another day type.
data_description.base_day_set: Start from that day type's dates — e.g. Monday, to build "first Monday of the month" without a calendar.
data_description.base_calendars: e.g. the trash-collection calendar. Not needed for holidays — see below.
data_description.holidays_country: ISO code such as US, CA, GB. Public holidays are computed here — no Workday integration or holiday calendar needed.
data_description.holidays_subdiv: Optional, e.g. IL for Illinois-only holidays.
data_description.holidays_observed: On: a holiday falling on Saturday counts on Friday, Sunday on Monday — as federal offices do.
data_description.holidays_remove: Pick the ones that are ordinary days for you (Columbus Day, Veterans Day…). The list fills in after the country is saved once.

cancelled.name: Cancelled — what takes a day back out

data.exclude_match: Only cancel when the entry's title has

data_description.exclude_day_sets: Their dates are removed. Workday = Mon–Fri minus Holiday; Day Off = Mon–Fri minus Workday.
data_description.exclude_calendars: e.g. your own calendar, with a tag rule below.
data_description.exclude_match: A word or tag matched against an event's TITLE, whole words only — #do does not match #done, and notes are not read. A bare word applies to every calendar in this tier; a line like `calendar.anderson: #do` applies to that calendar only (one rule per line, or separated by ;). Leave empty to cancel on any entry.

data.force_match: Only force when the entry's title has

data_description.force_calendars: These win over everything, including the cancellations above.
data_description.force_match: Same rules as above — e.g. `calendar.anderson: #wd` so a tagged entry makes a day a workday after all.

pick.name: Pick — narrow to a cadence, an ordinal, or certain months
pick.description: Both kinds of pick count ELIGIBLE dates, not calendar days: "every other trash day" follows a holiday shift, and "last workday of the month" is holiday-aware.

data_description.pick_every: For "every Nth". Every 3rd day on Daily; every 14th day from a Tuesday is every other Tuesday.
data_description.pick_anchor: Required for "every Nth". The first eligible date on or after it starts the count; nothing before it is included.
data_description.months: Applied after the pick. "First Monday" plus November gives the first Monday of November.

data.invert: Invert (every date NOT in this day type)
data.expose_calendar: Show in the HA calendar panel

data_description.invert: Every date that is not in the rule above.
data_description.offset_days: Moves every date. -1 gives "the night before"; +1 after the first Monday of November gives Election Day. Applied last.
data_description.expose_calendar: Publishes this day type as a calendar entity. Off is right for a helper like "every other Tuesday" that nobody needs to see. It stays selectable in the card either way.

pick_remove.title: Remove a day type
pick_remove.description: Its calendar entity is removed too. Schedules using it, and day types built on it or subtracting it, will stop matching.

error.invalid_dates: Could not read those dates. Use YYYY-MM-DD, separated by commas, with ranges written as YYYY-MM-DD..YYYY-MM-DD.
error.base_cycle: That day type builds on, or subtracts, this one (directly or through others), which would loop forever.
error.base_missing: That day type no longer exists.

abort.unknown_day_set: That day type no longer exists.
